title: Session-level Token Exposure Oracle: deterministic cost exposure for multi-route requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: multi-route and conversational requests currently produce fragmented token records across the streaming gateway and model routers. Downstream cost attribution jobs consume these fragments and heuristically stitch them, causing non-deterministic per-session exposure numbers that leak into invoices and cost dashboards. We need a deterministic, idempotent stage that computes canonical "exposed tokens" per session/request that downstream billing, dashboards, and reserved-capacity chargebacks can trust.

Goal: implement a session-level Token Exposure Oracle (TEO) service that materializes a single canonical exposure record per logical request/session. The TEO will: (1) ingest event streams from the gateway (request-start, chunk-emit, route-assignment, model-response, fallback) and router acknowledgements, (2) compute token exposure with stable tie-breaking for concurrent shards and multi-model fanout, (3) emit idempotent exposure events to the billing topic (kafka:billing.exposures.v1) and write a compact canonical row to BigQuery for downstream joins and audits.

Non-goals: replacing the existing ledger, reworking billing pricing math, or performing retroactive invoice adjustments in this ticket. Those are follow-ups once canonical exposure is available.
acceptance_criteria: TEO consumes gateway/router event streams and emits one canonical exposure event per logical request id within 5s of request completion
Canonical exposure record includes: request_id, session_id, tenant_id, route_ids, model_variants, token_count_total, token_breakdown_by_source, confidence_flags, canonical_timestamp, event_version
Idempotency: re-processing the same upstream events must not create duplicate canonical rows (dedupe by event_version + request_id)
Shock test: under 5x normal throughput the TEO must maintain 99.9% emission success with <1% event lag beyond 10s in staging
Backfill path: historical fragmented token events can be run through a batch converter job to emit canonical rows (separate backfill task documented)
Downstream billing consumers can subscribe to kafka:billing.exposures.v1 and reconcile totals against existing ledger within 0.1% for a 24h sample (verification job provided)
Telemetry: traces, per-tenant failure counts, and a Grafana panel showing lag/duplicates/failed-emits.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — ingested sample gateway +/- router events in local harness and prototyped a deterministic tie-breaker that orders fanout by (route_priority, model_size, router_shard, offset)
2026-02-28: Data contract drafted and reviewed with Billing PM (link below). Expanded canonical schema to include confidence_flags and event_version to support future variants

2026-03-03: Prototype service implemented in go using confluent-kafka-go and a compact RocksDB local cache for in-flight windowing. End-to-end test harness running in CI with synthetic fanout patterns

2026-03-08: Design review with infra and security. Decided to keep emitted canonical rows in append-only topic and rely on downstream compacting consumer to maintain final ledger rows. Security requested an audit log flag for high-privilege tenants

2026-03-10: Began integration tests against staging Kafka and BigQuery. Initial run shows 0.6% duplicate emissions caused by upstream connector retries; working on stronger dedupe keys and idempotent producer settings.
comments: Marco Rios (2026-02-25): Can we include route-level cost multipliers in the event so the billing job doesn't have to rehydrate routing decisions? Thinking about dedicated overrides.

Lena Morris (Billing PM) (2026-02-28): +1 on event_version, please also include tenant_billing_tier to help spot discrepancies between reserved and on-demand. We'll verify against reserved capacity reports.
Security (2026-03-08): Suggest storing PII-free session references only and a separate ACLed audit trail for full traceability. See confluence note.

Marco Rios (2026-03-10): Investigated duplicate emissions — root cause is connector exactly-once gap when upstream assigns different partition keys for the same request. Working on canonical partitioning to match request_id modulus to single partition.
review_feedback: Lena Morris (2026-03-02): Please add tenant_billing_tier and explicit reserved_capacity_flag to the canonical record so Billing can apply discounts without rehydrating the route history.

Priya Nair (Infra) (2026-03-08): RocksDB local cache is ok for prototype, but production should use a sharded in-memory window with periodic checkpointing to S3 for faster recovery. Also call out Kubernetes affinity for hot tenants.
risks_and_mitigation: Upstream duplicate events causing over-reporting — mitigate with event_version, canonical partitioning by request_id, and idempotent producer settings
Latency spikes under load — mitigation: circuit-break to emit per-route partial exposures with a 'partial=true' flag so billing can still proceed; follow-up job will compact partials
Schema drift between router/gateway — mitigation: strict schema registry with compatibility checks and a graceful disable path that routes to a diagnostic topic
next_steps: Complete dedupe fix and re-run staging integration (by 2026-03-14)
Add tenant_billing_tier and reserved_capacity_flag to canonical event and update docs (by 2026-03-18)
Run 24h staging reconciliation against ledger to validate <0.1% drift and publish results to Billing team (by 2026-03-21)
Schedule rollout plan: canary 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100% with shadow run for 3 days each
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to the canonicalization stage; any invoice corrections or customer notifications will be handled by separate billing ops playbooks after we validate outputs in staging.
